name: Loscil
label: Kranky
lede: Destroyer's old drummer named his project after a line of Csound code, mailed a demo to Chicago and spent the next quarter century turning Vancouver's rain, harbors and wildfire smoke into Kranky records.

eras.title: The drummer with a synthesis manual
eras.text: Scott Morgan grew up in Vancouver and Courtenay, studied under computer-music pioneer Barry Truax at Simon Fraser University, and played drums in Destroyer. On the side he started making ambient electronics inside a Vancouver multimedia collective.

years.h: Scott Morgan joins Dan Bejar's Destroyer on drums
years.p: Morgan plays drums, saxophone, clarinet and classical guitar in [[Destroyer|61604b45-8a91-4e33-a1b6-45d7b1fec4e5]] from 1998 to 2002, alongside [[Dan Bejar|9f142b12-570e-464d-9cb0-f1d579bb6a66]].

years.h: Loscil starts inside Vancouver's Multiplex collective
years.p: Scott Morgan launches Loscil while part of Multiplex, a collective running audiovisual nights at The Blinding Light, an underground cinema. The name comes from Csound's looping oscillator function.
years.xp: Csound is a sound synthesis programming language, and loscil is its instruction for playing a sampled sound in a loop. AllMusic reads the name as loop plus oscillate. Either way, it's a synthesis nerd's joke that became a career.

years.h: A New Demonstration of Thermodynamic Tendencies, self-released
years.p: Scott Morgan's first Loscil album is named after a physics textbook. The demo caught the ear of Chicago's Kranky.

eras.title: Physics, submarines and a night job in Destroyer
eras.text: Kranky turned the demo into a debut and Loscil became one of the label's steadiest names. Scott Morgan built each record around a concept, from thermodynamics to deep water, and still found time to rejoin Destroyer.

years.h: Triple Point: Loscil's Kranky debut
years.p: According to AllMusic, Kranky released Scott Morgan's thermodynamics demo as his official debut under a new title, Triple Point, in October 2001.

years.h: Submers: a whole Loscil album named for submarines
years.p: Scott Morgan's aquatic second Kranky album titles its tracks after submarines, turning dub pulses and drones into something you hear from under the hull.

years.h: Loscil music in the documentary The Corporation
years.p: Scott Morgan's music appears in the Canadian documentary, the first of many film and TV placements.

years.h: First Narrows brings in live players
years.p: Named for the Vancouver harbor channel under the Lions Gate Bridge, Loscil's third album adds live instruments. Wikipedia calls its tone poems more organic and looser than before.

years.h: Scott Morgan rejoins Destroyer
years.p: Morgan plays in [[Destroyer|61604b45-8a91-4e33-a1b6-45d7b1fec4e5]] again from 2005 to 2007. The vinyl of Destroyer's Rubies (2006) carries an extra track called Loscil's Rubies.

years.h: Plume: Loscil's fourth Kranky album
years.p: After the water of Submers, Scott Morgan's concepts climb into the air.

eras.title: Dan Bejar, video games and Vancouver's edges
eras.text: By day Scott Morgan worked as a sound director in video games; by night he made records about the city around him. Destroyer's Dan Bejar showed up on one, and Hollywood started licensing the rest.

years.h: Loscil scores the game Osmos
years.p: Scott Morgan's music soundtracks the hit indie game, while Strathcona Variations, named for a Vancouver neighborhood, comes out on Ghostly International.

years.h: Endless Falls: Dan Bejar speaks on The Making of Grief Point
years.p: Loscil's Kranky album closes with Destroyer's [[Dan Bejar|9f142b12-570e-464d-9cb0-f1d579bb6a66]] reading over Scott Morgan's music. Destroyer's Archer on the Beach EP the same year carries the spoken-word piece Grief Point, with music by Loscil.

years.h: Loscil soundtracks Prototype 2
years.p: Scott Morgan scores the open-world action game, a long way from the cinema basements where Loscil started. Sketches from New Brighton comes out on Kranky the same year.

years.h: Loscil music in Sofia Coppola's The Bling Ring
years.p: Scott Morgan's music lands in the heist film, and a year later in Divergent. He also makes Erebus with [[bvdub|94d43a2c-b5f5-4d02-988c-20332d1eebd3]] on Glacial Movements.

q: The nature is so beautiful but it's coupled with human intervention
years.h: Sea Island: nature reserves next to industry
years.p: Scott Morgan named the Kranky album after the Richmond, BC island that holds both Vancouver's airport and bird sanctuaries, and said that clash inspired it.
years.xp: Morgan told Exberliner that Vancouver was the ideal setting for his music, in an ironic way: the landscape is stunning, and it's never far from industry. That balance, he said, is what interests him musically.

eras.title: Apps, clouds and a Budapest string section
eras.text: Scott Morgan stretched Loscil into a generative app, a cello duo and film work for Netflix, then took his sound to a 22-piece orchestra. Clara became his best-reviewed record.

years.h: ADRIFT: Loscil as a generative app
years.p: Scott Morgan releases an app-album whose music is generated fresh each time it plays.

years.h: Monument Builders on Kranky
years.p: Seven tracks with titles like Drained Lake, Red Tide and Anthropocene, Loscil's darkest turn toward the human footprint on the landscape.

years.h: High Plains: Scott Morgan and cellist Mark Bridges
years.p: Morgan co-founds the duo High Plains with cellist Mark Bridges; their debut Cinderland is on Kranky. Loscil also scores Netflix's Suburra: Blood on Rome.

years.h: Equivalents: Loscil sets Stieglitz's cloud photos to sound
years.p: Scott Morgan's album takes its name and idea from Alfred Stieglitz's series of cloud photographs, premiered at MUTEK as an audiovisual show with heavy sub-bass.

years.h: Clara: Loscil works with a 22-piece Budapest string orchestra
years.p: Scott Morgan builds the Kranky album from recordings of a 22-piece string orchestra in Budapest. It scores 85 on Metacritic, his highest yet.

eras.title: Colours of air, lake fire
eras.text: Loscil's recent run pairs Scott Morgan with Australian sound artist Lawrence English and ends, so far, with a solo record named for fire on the water.

years.h: The Sails: two hours of Loscil dance scores
years.p: Scott Morgan self-releases a double album of music for choreographers, gathered from more than eight years of dance collaborations.

years.h: Colours of Air with Lawrence English
years.p: Scott Morgan and Brisbane's [[Lawrence English|eadd64ca-a4f8-4c0c-8405-fa46a7be2380]] make a Kranky album together; AllMusic says it drew wide acclaim.

years.h: Lake Fire: Loscil's first solo album since Clara
years.p: Nine tracks on Kranky, from Arrhythmia to Ash Clouds to the title piece, Scott Morgan's first solo Loscil record in four years.
